Recomputed on AED_HOUSE.DTA: uncentered VIFs (as chapter code) = size 40.13, bedrooms 57.82, bathrooms 34.74, lotsize 11.97, age 21.02, monthsold 12.80; correct centered VIFs (with sm.add_constant) = 1.69, 1.73, 1.30, 1.13, 1.18, 1.57 (max 1.73 — no multicollinearity, consistent with pairwise correlations ~0.5 and with L148's claim). Fixing the code flips the stated conclusion of the cell's output (warning branch -> 'Good: no serious multicollinearity') and invalidates Exercise 5's numbers, so per the fix-vs-report boundary this is action=report. Suggested repair (for Phase 2): add a constant column before computing VIF and report VIFs only for the non-constant regressors.
findings.verify_note: Recomputed: chapter code (X without add_constant) yields uncentered VIFs max 57.82, matching dump CELL 13's warning; centered VIFs max ~1.73. findings.summary: The AIC/BIC formulas use \widehat{\sigma}_e^2 without defining its divisor, while the only variance-like quantity the chapter defines (s_e, line 451) divides by n-k; the code actually uses RSS/n, so a one-line clarifier prevents students from plugging in s_e^2 and getting values that do not match the computed AIC = 675.48 / BIC = 685.05.
findings.old: $$\text{BIC} = n \times \ln(\widehat{\sigma}_e^2) + n(1 + \ln 2\pi) + k \times \ln(n)$$
findings.new:
$$\text{BIC} = n \times \ln(\widehat{\sigma}_e^2) + n(1 + \ln 2\pi) + k \times \ln(n)$$

where $\widehat{\sigma}_e^2 = \text{RSS}/n$ (note the divisor is $n$, not the $n-k$ used for $s_e$).
findings.evidence: Code at lines 497–499 computes aic_stata/bic_stata with np.log(rss/n); dump CELL 10 gives AIC 675.4824, BIC 685.0535, which Exercise 4 (lines 967–968) reuses as 675.5/685.1. Line 451 defines s_e with divisor n-k, so \widehat{\sigma}_e^2 is otherwise ambiguous within the chapter.
findings.verify_note: Code (L497-499) uses rss/n; s_e defined with n-k at L451; section-10.6 formula leaves σ̂_e² undefined. Clarifier 'σ̂_e² = RSS/n (divisor n, not n-k)' is mathematically correct (MLE/Stata convention) and reconciles with AIC 675.48 / BIC 685.05.

findings.summary: Key Concept 10.6 states BIC = n ln(sigma^2) + k ln(n), silently dropping the n(1+ln 2*pi) constant included in the section 10.6 formulas and in the code — so the KC formula would give 602.75, not the 685.05/685.1 the chapter and Exercise 4 report; a parenthetical reconciles the two.
findings.old: stronger penalties: BIC = $n \ln(\hat{\sigma}_e^2) + k \ln(n)$. Smaller
findings.new: stronger penalties: BIC = $n \ln(\hat{\sigma}_e^2) + k \ln(n)$ (omitting a constant that does not affect model comparisons). Smaller
findings.evidence: Section formula at line 483 and code at line 499 include n(1+ln 2*pi) = 82.30 for n=29; dump CELL 10 BIC = 685.0535, matching Exercise 4's 685.1. KC 10.6's version yields 685.05 - 82.30 = 602.75 — internally inconsistent presentation without the clarifier.
findings.verify_note: Verified: n(1+ln2π)=82.30 for n=29; KC 10.6's simplified BIC would give 685.05-82.30=602.75, inconsistent with Exercise 4's 685.1. The dropped term is constant across models on the same n, so 'omitting a constant that does not affect model comparisons' is accurate. Additive parenthetical is correct.

findings.summary: The R-squared properties list says R2 'Always increases when adding variables', which is inconsistent with the mathematically precise statement in Key Concept 10.13 ('can only increase or stay the same — it never decreases'); R2 is unchanged when the added regressor gets an exactly zero OLS coefficient.
findings.old: - **Problem:** Always increases when adding variables (even irrelevant ones)
findings.new: - **Problem:** Never decreases when adding variables (even irrelevant ones)
findings.evidence: Key Concept 10.13 (lines 1397–1399) states: 'When adding predictors to a regression model, $R^2$ can only increase or stay the same — it never decreases.' The weak-inequality version is the correct property (R2 stays constant iff the added regressor's OLS coefficient is exactly zero); harmonizing removes the internal inconsistency.
findings.verify_note: KC 10.13 (L1397-1399) states the precise 'never decreases / can only increase or stay the same'; L439's 'Always increases' is the internally inconsistent loose form. 'Never decreases' is the technically correct property (R² unchanged iff added regressor's OLS coef is exactly 0) and harmonizes the chapter. Also sharpens the contrast with the adjacent adjusted-R² bullet ('can decrease').
